explanation: Precompute downward heights and rightward widths. Scan from bottom-right: a true cell starts a square whose side is the minimum of its two runs and one plus the square starting diagonally below-right.
timeComplexity: O(rc): two complete cell scans with constant work per cell.
spaceComplexity: O(rc): height/width runs and square sides are stored for every cell.
attribution: Adapted reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/max_square_submatrix.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: A square starting at a cell consists of its top row, left column, and the square beginning one step diagonally inward. The two runs bound the first two parts; one plus the diagonal square side bounds the interior. Their minimum is therefore both feasible and maximal. Reverse traversal ensures these dependencies are known.
walkthrough: For [[true,true,false],[true,true,true],[false,true,true]], the diagonal square at (1,1) has side 2. At (0,0), the downward and rightward runs both have length 2, so min(2,2,1+2)=2. The largest area is 2²=4; false corners prevent side 3.
edgeCases: Return side squared, not the side length.
